title: The perceptron, activation functions, and what a layer actually computes

videos.script: A neural network sounds like a brain. On the screen it is a multiplication. {{matmul}} Sixty-four numbers come in, one per pixel of a small handwritten digit. Each is multiplied by a weight, the products are added, and a fixed function is applied to the sum. {{unit}} That is one unit. A layer is sixteen of them side by side, and it is one matrix product. {{layer}} The oldest version of this is the perceptron, from 1958. It learns AND from four examples in six passes. {{and}} It cannot learn XOR, however long you let it try. No straight line separates those four points. {{xor}} Two layers can. With weights set by hand, the second layer combines what the first one found, and XOR comes out right. {{two}} Between the layers sits a function that bends. Take it away, and two layers collapse into one. {{collapse}} Before any of that, this lesson builds the machine you will type on, with Python and PyTorch, on your own computer. {{lab}} Everything else in the course runs there. {{end}}
